Dr. Jose Jiminez
Melbourne Private Hospital
19 Grange Road
Melbourne 3000

22/01/2007

Dear Doctor,
Re: Mrs. Ann Howard, aged 36

Thank you for seeing Mrs. Howard, who presented with signs of early abdominal obstruction. Her
condition requires your urgent attention.

Today, Mrs. Howard presented with no passage of stools or flatus. Her abdomen is tense, there are      Commented [DSM1]: was
quiet bowel sounds and her full blood examination revealed reduced hemoglobin and mild left            Commented [DSM2]: were
shift.

Initially on 20/01/2007, Mrs. Howard had complained of sudden onset sharp pain in the left lower
abdomen, which worsened on sitting, standing or bending. She denied having any nausea,
vomiting, change in bowel habits, urinary symptoms or weight loss. On the examination, there was
notable tenderness and a vague mass in the left lower quadrant, together with a slightly elevated
pulse and blood pressure. Over the next three days, the pain has persisted, particularly worse after
eating, and she has been passing hard stools coated with bright red blood.

Mrs. Howard reported that she had complained of abdominal pain on 18/12/2006, which might
have been related to spontaneous abortion. Her past surgical history is notable for appendectomy
and ovarian cystectomy.

In light of the above, I would be grateful for your thoughts on how to manage her condition. Thank
you for your anticipated cooperation.

If you need more information, please contact me. [do not forget this sentence]

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
